pass_b_english: …others, Satan is called a strong city, and this is strong; for it is the custom of the God-inspired Scripture to liken the very strong to towers, walls, or cities, as we have previously said. As the blessed prophet Jeremiah said, God sets up a strong city and a bronze wall (Jeremiah 1:10). Once the Emmanuel was revealed to the world, the unholy crowd of opposing powers was lifted, and Satan was shaken from his depths; he has fallen in such a way that he is unable to rise or breathe again, and he does not expect to recover at any time.

Therefore, the poor people will bless you, and the cities of oppressed men will bless you. For you became a helper to every humble city, and a refuge to those who were despairing due to poverty, rescuing them from wicked men; a shelter for the thirsty, and a spirit for men of wrongdoing. They will bless you as people who are faint-hearted and thirsty; in Zion, from wicked men to whom you delivered us.

Israel was called to the knowledge of God through the pedagogy of the law, and was enriched by the things from God. For he was saved, and inherited the land of promise. The multitude of other nations, being immeasurable, is completely alien to spiritual goods; they are unprotected and without divine gifts, destitute and without shelter in a certain way, lacking the divine covering, lacking the wealth of virtue, and lacking anything worthy of praise, and is unworthy of wonder. But when Christ appeared, he freed them from the devil's greed and brought them to God, and they were enriched with the light of truth and the glory of the gospel; therefore, they send up joyful songs to God and the Father regarding the greatness of the evangelical polity.

O Lord, you made an ancient and true plan, summing up all things in Christ, and you enlightened those in darkness while overthrowing the rulers of this age; and just as certain cities are strong, the poor people will bless you, and all cities will glorify you. For you have become a helper to all, and a shelter to those afflicted by poverty regarding the ancestral goods, rescuing them from wicked men. For some were faint-hearted in Zion, like people thirsting, as we have previously said. And perhaps through these things the prophet shows us that there were those in Israel who thirsted for the Savior's presence, and for the Savior of all…
